title: Edge cases for unicode and international text
when: An app stores, searches, sorts, counts or shows user text, and the user wants it tested with accents, emoji, other scripts and right to left text.
inputs: where text is entered, stored and shown
prompt:
Goal: A check that text survives the full path (input, storage, search, sort, limits, display) in any script, with failing examples.
Steps:
1. Encoding at every layer: meta charset utf-8, files saved as UTF-8, server Content-Type with charset, Python open with encoding="utf-8".
2. Test strings: a name with tilde and cedilla, a German sharp s, a Japanese phrase, a family emoji, an Arabic sentence with digits.
3. Length: compare str.length with the grapheme count from Intl.Segmenter for limits and truncation; never cut inside a surrogate pair.
4. Normalization: precomposed and decomposed accents must match in search and uniqueness; apply normalize("NFC") on input.
5. Search and sort: accent and case insensitive search with localeCompare and sensitivity: "base"; Intl.Collator for name sorting.
6. Direction and escaping: dir="auto" on user content; < & and quotes stay literal in HTML, CSV and JSON.
Quality bar:
- Each finding shows the string and its code points.
- Truncation never splits a character.
- Fixes use built in APIs (Intl, normalize).
Pitfalls:
- ASCII only test data.
- Comparing with toUpperCase.
- slice cutting an emoji in half.
Verify:
- [ ] Encoding set at every layer.
- [ ] Limits checked with grapheme counts.
- [ ] Normalization tested.
- [ ] Right to left display checked.
Output: unicode-qa.md with test strings, results and fixes.

examples.input: nomes com acento e emoji estao quebrando na lista
examples.output: search for Jose misses the accented form (NFD stored), 20 char limit cuts a family emoji; fix NFC and Intl.Segmenter
